conf.description: Palo Alto NGFW Threat log (syslog-csv, PAN-OS 10.2/11.1), direct route: positional CSV parse of the 12 mapped columns, threatid name/id split, severity string->numeric lookup, url.original gated by subtype, keep _raw per recommendations.direct.cribl (threat events are IDS-class/forensically worth the bytes)

conf.comment: Palo Alto NGFW Threat log, syslog-csv, direct route. Positions 1-31 (subtype=5, time_generated=7, src=8, dst=9, rule=12, app=15, sport=25, dport=26, proto=30, action=31) cross-checked against the live palo_alto_traffic reference pipeline and this dir's own traffic__syslog-csv.json (same field offsets through Action). Positions 32-35 (misc/threatid/category/severity) are the next four fields per the published PAN-OS Threat Log Fields doc, unverified against a live sample threat record. event.outcome is intentionally NOT derived here - recommendations.direct.cribl assigns that to the Elastic-side logs-panw.threat@custom pipeline for this format, unlike the CEF/LEEF formats whose own field-level transform explicitly asks for it in Cribl.

functions.description: Pipeline purpose, position provenance, and the event.outcome scope note
Positional capture of subtype(5), time_generated(7) and the 12 work-order Threat columns through severity(35)

Split the composite threatid into numeric id + description, map severity vocabulary to the numeric ECS scale, and gate misc into url.original only for the url subtype - all BEFORE rename, reading the flat vendor field names
Batch rename of every mapped/custom (no-transform) column; threatid deliberately excluded so its combined raw value survives for the cross-reference pipelines
Set _time from the CSV Generated Time column (field 7); Elastic destination maps _time onward to @timestamp
Tag event.dataset; drop now-consumed parse scratch (subtype/time_generated/misc/severity). _raw and threatid are deliberately kept.
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
